title: VoltForge AI local model master backlog
scope: Voltforge_AI plus the minimum Voltforge_BL and Voltforge_UI integration required to operate the project-owned model

productDecision.generationModel: A VoltForge-owned decoder language model trained from random initialization with a VoltForge-owned tokenizer and dataset pipeline
productDecision.thirdPartyModelPolicy: No hosted model API, no external inference provider, no pretrained model weights, and no pretrained tokenizer are permitted in the generation path
productDecision.internetPolicy: Internet access is an optional evidence-retrieval tool only. Retrieved text is untrusted context, never a replacement model and never authority without a citation.
productDecision.reliabilityPolicy: Deterministic circuit, firmware, compiler, simulation, and safety tools remain authoritative. The language model explains and synthesizes their verified outputs.
productDecision.memoryPolicy: Only bounded, user-visible project/session memory is allowed. Hidden chain-of-thought, secrets, and unapproved cross-project training data are prohibited.
productDecision.implementationFreeze: No further model/runtime implementation should begin until this backlog is reviewed. Each implementation phase must satisfy its exit gate before the next phase starts.

observations: The current model/artifacts/config.json describes a 4,096-token vocabulary, 128-token context, 64-dimensional, 2-layer model; it is a very small experiment, not a production domain LLM.
The current model_meta.json reports validation loss 8.295, which is not an acceptable release-quality result.
The VoltForge-1B files describe or randomly initialize an approximately 1.036B-parameter architecture, but no validated trained 1B checkpoint exists.
The reported 1B loss 10.826 and perplexity about 22,026 are unusable and must not be presented as a trained production model.
The current inference and reasoning paths mix experimental neural code, deterministic templates, and optimistic loaded-state reporting.
Provider-oriented code introduced during the previous migration attempt conflicts with the local-only product decision and must be removed.
Existing circuit validation, firmware review, SSE relay, request bounds, and UI context work may be retained only after local-only review and tests.
rules: Never report an architecture manifest as a trained model.
Never randomly initialize a missing production checkpoint at service startup.
Never mark a model loaded when tokenizer, tensor shapes, checksums, or compatibility checks fail.
Never use parameter count as a quality claim.
Preserve legacy artifacts until they are inventoried; quarantine them from production rather than silently deleting evidence.

correctness: Zero critical safety false negatives on the release-blocking deterministic fixture set.
At least 95% pin/wiring mismatch detection on the held-out supported-board set.
At least 97% electronics-domain boundary accuracy and out-of-domain refusal accuracy.
At least 90% first-pass compile success for supported, fixture-backed generated firmware tasks and at least 97% after one verified repair pass.
100% valid public API envelopes after schema validation or explicit fallback; malformed model text is never returned as a typed action.
grounding: Every web-derived factual claim includes source URL, source title, retrieval time, and evidence excerpt identifier.
At least 95% citation entailment on the held-out retrieval evaluation set.
Missing or conflicting evidence is stated as uncertainty; no default voltage, pin, rating, or library API is fabricated.
performance: Reference hardware and measurement commands are published before model profile selection.
The selected local profile remains within its measured RAM/VRAM budget under maximum supported context.
Streaming cancellation, request deadlines, concurrency limits, and warm-up behavior pass load tests.
Quantization is accepted only when the domain score regression is within the approved threshold.
privacyAndSecurity: Project and conversation memory is isolated by authenticated user, project, and session.
Secrets and hidden reasoning are not persisted, trained on, emitted, or logged.
Web retrieval blocks private network targets, oversized responses, unsafe content types, redirects outside policy, and prompt-injection instructions.
All model-proposed project changes require a visible diff, matching project revision, explicit user approval, and undo support.

items.title: Optimize inference without hiding quality loss
items.work: Measure KV caching, attention kernels, dynamic batching, thread settings, memory mapping, and local int8/int4 quantization. Keep an unquantized reference and compare every optimization against the frozen suite.
definitionOfDone: Each optimization has before/after quality, latency, throughput, and memory evidence.
The released format is portable across declared hardware tiers.
Optimization fallback and artifact rollback are tested.

implementation.summary: Implemented an explicit, signed Gen1 inference-optimization contract and measured ten fresh-process CPU candidates against an unoptimized FP32/manual-attention/no-KV reference. Selected FP32 SDPA with unexpanded GQA KV caching and four Torch threads, retained FP32 manual attention plus KV caching as the signed fallback, added runtime-selected profile loading and safe fallback, packaged the unchanged weights/tokenizer as a new inactive immutable artifact, and rejected unportable or non-material candidates without hiding their quality, latency, throughput, or memory results.
evidence: The offline benchmark independently re-verifies and loads the signed 14,198,464-parameter artifact for every candidate, denies outbound network access, evaluates all 9,027 targets in immutable split vf-tokenizer-split-v1, and repeats four eight-token greedy probes derived from the frozen VFAI-005 suite. It stores source/prompt/output hashes but no raw prompt or generated text.

The explicit reference profile uses FP32, manual attention, four Torch threads, no KV cache, no memory map, and batch size one. It measured validation loss 5.9367194, perplexity 378.690557321, top-1 accuracy 1.9386286%, 774.1903 ms median generation, 91.352 ms median first-token time, 41.333507 generated tokens/second, and 56,793,856 resident model-tensor bytes.

KV caching preserved validation loss, top-1 accuracy, and exact greedy token output while reducing median generation latency 50.400838%, reducing first-token time 7.949361%, and increasing throughput 101.616309% versus the unoptimized reference with no change in resident model-tensor bytes.

PyTorch scaled-dot-product attention on top of KV caching preserved the complete frozen validation metrics and exact greedy tokens while reducing median generation latency another 4.815701%, reducing first-token time 4.973594%, and increasing throughput 5.059344% versus the manual-attention KV baseline. The selected profile measured 365.5 ms median generation, 79.9078 ms first-token time, and 87.5513 tokens/second.

Memory mapping preserved quality but improved throughput only 0.978248% and worsened first-token latency 0.575811%, so it failed the material-improvement gate. One and eight threads regressed throughput by 10.993053% and 13.874118%; two threads improved throughput only 2.463663% while worsening first-token time 9.50754%. Four threads remain selected.

Dynamic batch size four preserved quality and exact outputs and measured 225.193367 tokens/second, 170.226341% above the single-request KV baseline, with 142.1001 ms median batch generation. It remains measurement-only because the current service has no cancellation/deadline-aware batching scheduler; later API integration owns that scheduler rather than silently enabling unsafe request coalescing.

Portable local weight-only int8 and int4 probes preserved exact greedy outputs on this matrix and changed validation loss by -0.000665% and +0.036065%, while reducing resident tensor storage 65.085575% to 19,829,248 bytes and 77.580448% to 12,732,928 bytes. They were rejected because throughput regressed 48.368803% and 72.70792%, first-token time regressed 55.911457% and 154.200197%, and the implementations are CPU-only. No quantized weight format is released.

The selected release-format boundary remains portable FP32 pytorch-weights-only-state-dict-v1. CPU is the required measured tier; CUDA and MPS are explicitly conditional-unmeasured rather than claimed. VFAI-FU-007 records the owned-hardware accelerator benchmark that this CPU-only Windows host cannot execute honestly.

items.work: Validate domain scope, output schema, citations, unsupported claims, dangerous instructions, repetition, truncation, and confidence proxies before returning model output. Use deterministic responses when neural output fails.

implementation.summary: Implemented a fail-closed neural generation boundary with a checksum-bound policy, strict typed JSON envelope, electronics-domain and lexical evidence support checks, exact citations, confidence caps, dangerous-instruction, repetition, and truncation rejection, canonical proposal-only action validation, one deterministic fallback resolver, visible SSE fallback metadata, and privacy-safe health counters. It accepts only a bounded exact-field UTF-8 JSON envelope and constructs visible text, citations, and the typed inference-response record only after every gate passes; rejected decisions contain no response text, typed response, or action.

Grounded claims must remain in VoltForge electronics scope, cite existing complete/reported typed evidence, have lexical support in the cited evidence, and exactly match the envelope citation set. Code fixes require compiled evidence. Unknown fields and hidden auto-apply controls fail the canonical task contract before any typed action can cross the boundary.

The resolver has only two outcomes: a fully accepted neural response or the existing deterministic electronics engine. implementation.summary: Implemented a checksum-bound, exact-token project context compiler that canonicalizes every requested VoltForge project source into the shared typed task-record prompt, selects complete sections by deterministic safety-aware priority, fails closed on incompatible context windows, exposes privacy-safe compilation metadata through chat and health routes, and keeps all current 128-token experimental artifacts inactive.

ProjectContextCompiler normalizes board, components, pins, wires, netlist, active selection, firmware files, diagnostics, simulation state, recent memory, retrieved evidence, and deterministic tool output. implementation.summary: Implemented a versioned, offline, deterministic engineering authority spanning seven typed local tools; bound every finding to evidence, severity, affected project IDs, and a reviewable fix; integrated the report through context compilation, quality gating, FastAPI, Spring DTOs, and UI types; and made critical output non-overridable by deterministic fallback or any future local neural response.

items.title: Add secure optional internet evidence retrieval
items.work: Implement a separately configured search/retrieval client with approved providers/domains, strict time/size limits, safe URL resolution, cache TTL, content sanitization, source timestamps, and an explicit offline/degraded state.
definitionOfDone: Search is used only when requested or when local evidence is insufficient under a documented policy.
Private/reserved IP ranges, arbitrary user URL fetching, unsafe redirects, binary content, and prompt-injection instructions are blocked.
Search failure never blocks local tools/model and never triggers invented fallback facts.
No web content enters the training corpus without separate provenance and licensing approval.

implementation.summary: Replaced the unrestricted HTML scraper and indefinite disk cache with a checksum-pinned, opt-in JSON evidence service that owns provider selection, trigger policy, DNS/IP and URL validation, redirect/proxy/content/size boundaries, sanitization, prompt-injection rejection, bounded sanitized-only TTL caching, source timestamps, typed citations, explicit offline/degraded states, and fail-open continuation to local deterministic/model paths.
evidence: internet_retrieval/policy.v1.json pins policy SHA-256 3a7a34e0610fafc361ff4fb979e0bd49d3cfbd362413adb408ddf4ddd380c37c, exactly one provider endpoint (https://api.duckduckgo.com/), its domain/path/query/content-type allowlists, zero redirects/retries, no environment proxies, a 262,144-byte response ceiling, four-result ceiling, 900-second default sanitized cache TTL, and explicit no-generation/no-training trust rules.

InternetRetrievalQuery accepts bounded search text and result count only; no URL, endpoint, provider, method, host, path, port, redirect, or content-type field is accepted from a caller. Historical datasheet and reasoning callers now delegate through this contract, and the former BeautifulSoup HTML scraping and disk cache are removed.

Every provider request is internally constructed as credential-free HTTPS, checked against the exact provider allowlist, resolved before use, and rejected if any DNS answer is private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT, multicast, reserved, unspecified, or otherwise non-global. Requests disable environment proxies, redirects, retries, and implicit body buffering.

The transport accepts only approved JSON media types, validates Content-Length, streams and caps decompressed bytes, decodes strict UTF-8, requires an object JSON root, and converts timeout, DNS, status, redirect, content, size, and format failures into content-free degraded responses.

Provider result URLs are sanitized HTTPS citations only and are never fetched. Markup/control characters are removed, whitespace is normalized, unsafe citation URLs are discarded, instruction-like prompt injection causes the entire result to be rejected, and only bounded sanitized title/snippet/source metadata can enter cache or model context.

Search runs only for documented explicit internet phrases or when VFAI-022 reports no-results/unavailable and the request has a documented evidence intent such as datasheet, pinout, specifications, release notes, current version, part number, or library API. All other requests return not-requested without DNS or HTTP; a disabled deployment returns offline explicitly.

Each accepted item carries stable evidence/citation IDs, provider identity, source URL/domain, retrieval timestamp, optional publication timestamp field, content SHA-256, retrieved authority, untrusted/sanitized flags, promptInjectionDetected=false, and trainingUseAllowed=false. Cache entries contain only this sanitized contract and expire deterministically by TTL and bounded LRU count.

implementation.summary: Implemented an opt-in, authenticated, pseudonymous SQLite memory system for project facts, decisions, summaries, and redacted recent-turn summaries. Expired entries are purged and over-limit entries are evicted deterministically by scope, kind priority, creation time, and stable memory ID.

The chat boundary discards all client-provided memory and injects only enabled, authenticated, revision-current server-managed entries. items.title: Build governed feedback and retraining loops
items.work: Collect explicit useful/incorrect/unsafe feedback linked to request and artifact versions, route it to review, convert approved failures into non-leaking evaluation/training examples, and schedule reproducible retraining rather than live self-modification.
definitionOfDone: The production model never changes weights from live chats.
Feedback requires project access and stores only approved bounded evidence.
Regression examples enter the held-out suite before they may enter a later training set.
Every retrained candidate repeats all release gates.

implementation.summary: Added a project-scoped, fail-closed feedback queue and two-stage review workflow. Feedback is bounded approved evidence linked to request, response, project revision, artifact, and registry identities; it never accepts or stores raw prompts, raw responses, or project snapshots. Approved regressions enter a private held-out set before a separately consented non-leaking training example may be scheduled.
evidence: feedback_governance/policy.v1.json defines useful/incorrect/unsafe kinds, pending/rejected/held-out/training-approved states, bounded fields, project access, explicit evidence approval, training consent, leakage, and no-live-mutation rules.

feedback_governance/service.py stores hashed user/project scope keys in SQLite, rejects secrets/instruction-like/project-snapshot evidence, emits content-free public summaries, creates immutable held-out regression records, checks the frozen and admitted held-out suite, and writes deterministic retraining candidate inputs and provenance manifests.
The API feedback route requires X-Voltforge-User-Id and matching X-Voltforge-Project-Id gateway headers; old transcript fields are rejected by the strict request contract.

tools/manage_feedback.py provides bounded health, review, held-out admission, training approval, scheduling, and run verification commands. Scheduling does not execute training, load weights, mutate live chats, or change the model registry.

A scheduled run binds feedback/held-out/training hashes, base artifact and registry revision, current runtime/API/data/tokenizer/retrieval compatibility, deterministic seed, hyperparameters, dependency checksums, and the required VFAI-032/VFAI-033 release gates.
